Chapter
	XIII
NOT	AT	HOME
In	the	meanwhile,	the	dwarves	sat	in	darkness,	and	utter
silence	 fell	 about	 them.	 Little	 they	 ate	 and	 little	 they
spoke.	They	could	not	count	the	passing	of	time;	and	they
scarcely	 dared	 to	 move,	 for	 the	 whisper	 of	 their	 voices
echoed	and	rustled	in	the	tunnel.	If	they	dozed,	they	woke
still	to	darkness	and	to	silence	going	on	unbroken.	At	last
after	days	and	days	of	waiting,	as	it	seemed,	when	they
were	 becoming	 choked	 and	 dazed	 for	 want	 of	 air,	 they
could	 bear	 it	 no	 longer.	 They	 would	 almost	 have
welcomed	sounds	from	below	of	the	dragon’s	return.	In
the	silence	they	feared	some	cunning	devilry	of	his,	but
they	could	not	sit	there	for	ever.
Thorin	 spoke:	 “Let	 us	 try	 the	 door!”	 he	 said.	 “I	 must
feel	 the	 wind	 on	 my	 face	 soon	 or	 die.	 I	 think	 I	 would
rather	be	smashed	by	Smaug	in	the	open	than	suffocate	in
here!”	So	several	of	the	dwarves	got	up	and	groped	back
to	where	the	door	had	been.	But	they	found	that	the	upper
end	 of	 the	 tunnel	 had	 been	 shattered	 and	 blocked	 with
broken	 rock.	 Neither	 key	 nor	 the	 magic	 it	 had	 once
obeyed	would	ever	open	that	door	again.
“We	are	trapped!”	they	groaned.	“This	is	the	end.	We
shall	die	here.”
